blocks.en: Caden Wu, Elizabeth Wong, Ian Cheng, Katherine Chen, Oscar Huang, Bruce Tsai

Chars Hsieh, an experienced researcher with over ten years of expertise in molecular and cell biology. I train and empower students at GEMS Academy, journeying with them to explore the frontiers of synthetic biology.
blocks.zh: Chars Hsieh，擁有逾十年分子與細胞生物學研究經驗的資深研究員。我在 GEMS Academy 培育並賦能學生，與他們一同探索合成生物學的前沿。
乾實驗指導老師

blocks.en: Each student advisor turned a year of experience into something the team did not have: an education site that strings our teaching work together across the years, the logistics and software behind advanced peptide design, a firmer structure for our videos, a photography initiative that puts plant stress in front of a global audience, and lab technique passed down bench to bench.
blocks.zh: 每一位學生顧問都把自己一年的經驗，變成隊伍原本沒有的東西：一個把我們歷年教學工作串起來的教育網站、進階胜肽設計背後的統籌與軟體、我們影片更紮實的架構、一項把植物逆境帶到全球觀眾眼前的攝影計畫，以及在實驗檯之間一代一代傳下來的實驗技術。

blocks.en: Each subteam has a lead, and some have a vice lead beside them. They planned the week's work, kept the lab, the model and the outreach moving at the same time, and were the first people the rest of us asked when something went wrong.
blocks.zh: 每一個分組都有一位負責人，有些組旁邊還有一位副負責人。他們安排每週的工作，讓實驗室、模型與對外推廣同時往前走，也是其他人一出狀況最先去問的人。

blocks.en: Greetings, I'm Ethan, and I initially joined iGEM because I wanted to see how to use synthetic biology to make a global impact. Throughout my journey, I have been met with many obstacles, including balancing the work-heavy duties I need to fulfil along with my academics. In the end, I learned to balance everything with a to-do list to keep track of my objectives and deadlines to ensure qualitative output in a timely manner. Now, I can do miniprep, colony PCR, gel electrophoresis, gel extraction, and many more experiments than when I began. iGEM is really special because it offers the chance for students to connect with professors in the field and for students to pitch their ideas to someone who knows the field well to hear thoughts from someone who can envision the future of the project. Presenting our project to the professors can be really nerve-wracking, but it felt good to experience it now than later, because I get to practice without any stakes. The professors were all really helpful and patient towards the team and each professor visit felt like someone else supported the team to keep going forward. Some professors offered seeds, while others offered products to test on. I think that to be able to experience this warmth in a year-long STEM project is very rare and priceless to me. One research question was "which protectant to use?" At first, I thought it was a really straightforward answer, but I later found that there were many factors to decide what was 'the best' for the team's objective in this project. I grabbed onto whatever was around me, trying to grab a sense of contribution to the team by doing broad research for candidates and submitting them for the instructors to review. I was so intrigued by the possibilities of candidates. I wanted to explore the boundaries of candidates we could use: maybe some novel ones, or maybe something between novel and well-established. After months of research, we ended up with a few prominent candidates that the instructors were pleased with (like ACCD and AtLEA14).
blocks.zh: 你好，我是 Ethan，一開始加入 iGEM 是想看看怎麼用合成生物學帶來全球性的影響。這一路上我遇到不少難關，包括如何在繁重的任務和課業之間取得平衡。最後我學會用待辦清單管理一切，追蹤自己的目標和截止期限，確保東西能按時做好、做得有品質。現在，比起剛開始的時候，我會做 miniprep、菌落 PCR、凝膠電泳、凝膠回收，還有更多實驗。iGEM 很特別，因為它讓學生有機會接觸這個領域的教授，把自己的想法向真正熟悉這個領域的人提案，聽聽看能夠預見這個專題未來的人怎麼想。向教授報告我們的專題其實很緊張，但現在就先經歷過比以後才經歷好，因為我可以在沒有壓力的情況下練習。這些教授都非常樂於幫忙、對隊伍很有耐心，每一次拜訪都像是又多了一個人支持隊伍繼續往前。有的教授提供種子，有的提供產品讓我們測試。能在一個為期一年的 STEM 專題裡感受到這樣的溫度，對我來說非常罕見，也非常珍貴。其中一個研究問題是「該用哪一種保護劑？」一開始我以為答案很直接，後來才發現要判斷什麼對隊伍在這個專題裡的目標才是「最好的」，牽涉到很多因素。我抓住手邊的一切，廣泛蒐集候選物並交給指導老師審查，想在隊伍裡抓住一點貢獻感。候選物的各種可能性讓我非常著迷。我想探索我們能用的候選物的邊界：也許是一些全新的，也許是介於全新與成熟之間的。經過數個月的研究，我們最後收斂到幾個指導老師也滿意的重點候選物（例如 ACCD 和 AtLEA14）。

blocks.en: Hello! I am Jessie, HP instructor. I've spent years teaching Chemistry and guiding various science projects. I enjoyed so much seeing students apply what they've learned to the real world, can't wait to see the impact this year's iGEM team will have on society!
blocks.zh: 哈囉！我是 Jessie，HP 指導老師。多年來我致力於教授化學並帶領各種科學計畫。看到學生將所學應用於現實世界讓我非常有成就感，非常期待看到今年 iGEM 隊伍對社會所帶來的影響！

blocks.en: Hello! I am Sophia and I joined iGEM to explore the field of synthetic biology and to acquire useful skills for my future science-related work. Coming into this project, I thought that I would only practice lab skills, but I have learned so much more regarding research, molecular dynamics, video making, and others! Through this experience, I also learned interpersonal skills such as leadership, team-building, time management, and communication. One of my favorite events was the Farmer's Expo where we were able to understand farmers' perspective on our project, allowing us to adapt to their needs. Because I struggled at the start to connect the dots between different aspects of our project, I shifted my focus to cross-team work, which is how I began to understand the importance of connecting the team together. The most rewarding part about iGEM was the inspiration and advice I gained from experts, farmers, instructors, and the team itself. Outside of iGEM, I like to spend my time staring down math problems, teaching children about science, discovering new cat cafes, taking photos, making a new playlist for every genre in every language, and singing my heart out in karaoke! I am so glad that iGEM provided me with the opportunity to explore some of these areas as well. Overall, iGEM showed me that working together as a team is what makes ideas become reality. I hope that our project's contribution to agriculture can empower farmers, allowing them to have the resources they need to protect their plants!
blocks.zh: 哈囉！我是 Sophia，加入 iGEM 是為了探索合成生物學這個領域，也為了替未來與科學相關的工作累積實用的技能。剛進這個專題的時候，我以為自己只會練習實驗技術，結果學到的遠不只這些：研究方法、分子動力學、影片製作等等！這段經歷也讓我學到領導、團隊建立、時間管理和溝通這些與人相處的能力。我最喜歡的活動之一是農民市集，我們在那裡了解農友怎麼看我們的專題，也因此能照著他們的需要調整。因為一開始我很難把專題各個面向的點連起來，我把重心轉到跨組工作，也就是從那時候開始，我才明白把整個隊伍串在一起有多重要。iGEM 最有收穫的部分，是我從專家、農友、指導老師以及隊伍本身得到的啟發和建議。iGEM 之外，我喜歡花時間和數學題目對看、教小朋友科學、發掘新的貓咖啡廳、拍照、替每一種語言的每一種曲風做新的播放清單，還有在 KTV 唱到盡興！我很高興 iGEM 也給了我探索其中一些領域的機會。整體來說，iGEM 讓我看到，把想法變成現實靠的是整支隊伍一起努力。我希望我們的專題對農業的貢獻能讓農友更有力量，讓他們拿到保護作物所需要的資源！

blocks.en: Hello! I'm Anna! When I first joined iGEM, all I knew was that I wanted to do something big, something that mattered. I didn't know how yet, but looking around a room full of strangers, I knew that together, we could. I still remember the first time I successfully produced a graph in RStudio for our math model. It felt foreign, but it showed me I could do more than I thought. From there, working through large geospatial datasets and leading conversations with farmers, I slowly came to understand the people we were working for: who they are, where they live, what they need, or simply what they had for lunch. I also began to see a clearer and clearer definition for what "something that mattered" means. I cherish the big wins: the opportunities to speak at a public forum, the thumbs-ups from strangers, the farmers smiling in my selfies. But I cherish the small moments just as much. There were the sighs my partners and I shared as our computers lagged under all that data, the laughter at lunch, and everything in between. ReLEAF ReLEAF ReLEAF: that's something to remember by!!
blocks.zh: 哈囉！我是 Anna！剛加入 iGEM 的時候，我只知道自己想做一件大事，一件有意義的事。我還不知道該怎麼做，但環顧一屋子的陌生人，我知道我們一起就可以。我還記得第一次成功用 RStudio 替我們的數學模型畫出圖的時候。那感覺很陌生，卻讓我看到自己能做的比想像中更多。從那裡開始，處理龐大的地理空間資料集、帶著和農友的對話，我慢慢認識了我們為之努力的那些人：他們是誰、住在哪裡、需要什麼，或只是中午吃了什麼。我也開始越來越清楚「有意義的事」到底是什麼意思。我珍惜那些大的時刻：在公開論壇上發言的機會、陌生人豎起的大拇指、自拍裡農友的笑容。但那些小的片刻我同樣珍惜。有我和夥伴看著電腦被那麼多資料拖慢時一起嘆的氣、午餐時的笑聲，以及這之間的一切。ReLEAF ReLEAF ReLEAF：這是值得記住的事！！

blocks.en: Hello, I'm Mia Guo! I first joined iGEM because I always had an interest in biology. Over this past year, I have made lesson plans for our education outreach, conducted research on professors, and hosted our public events in September. Moreover, through these preparations I have learned how to cooperate with large groups of people, public speaking, and also learning how to plan events and managing my time wisely. Looking back, this year has been fulfilling with many minor achievement scattered. I enjoyed achieving every milestone with the team and overall realized how much a group of high school students can achieve in just a few months. I am excited to present our project and go to Grand Jamboree!
blocks.zh: 哈囉，我是 Mia Guo！我最初加入 iGEM 是因為一直對生物學有興趣。過去這一年，我為我們的科學教育推廣寫教案、研究教授名單，也在九月主持了我們的公開活動。而且在這些準備過程中，我學會了怎麼和一大群人合作、怎麼公開演說，也學會規劃活動、聰明地安排自己的時間。回頭看，這一年很充實，散落著許多小小的成就。我很享受和隊伍一起達成每一個里程碑，也真正體會到一群高中生在短短幾個月裡能做到多少事。我很期待展示我們的專題，去 Grand Jamboree！

blocks.en: Hey I’m Abby Tsai! At first, I joined iGEM because I was intrigued by synthetic biology, wondering how far ONE year would actually bring us to. Now, looking back, it has been a wild journey. I stepped into the room full of strangers, not knowing in the year ahead, with this team, we’ll create so much memories while grinding and pouring our heart out into this project. In this team, I play roles in wetlab and plant modeling. Throughout the project I spent more than 300 hours in lab, and it has always been fascinating to operate on such tiny amount of reagents but able to produce for example, our optogenetic circuit. The results did not come from one day but months of failing and rebuilding. I'm proud to say I know how to do so many molecular cloning techniques now, where golden gate assembly or colony PCR being my favorite experiments. And why I say this whole year is a wild journey, I also grew teeny tiny arabidopsis, and treat them almost as if they’re my babies. This is also when I learned the art of patience as a farmers’ perspective: a little tilt, a little touch, a little movement all impacts their growth (or the mold just grows naughtily all over the agar plate). But that's fine, we became more careful and professional. Since each iGEM team is a heart merged by wetlab, drylab, and hp, I have been given the opportunity to pitch and present ideas to professors, to farmers, and even an iGEM co-founder; doing cross team bonding and side quests like designing clickers; but most importantly, to work with people with dynamic perspectives and backgrounds. The laughters shared will always be the highlight of my iGEM journey!
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Abby Tsai！一開始我加入 iGEM 是因為被合成生物學吸引，好奇一年到底能把我們帶到多遠。現在回頭看，這真是一趟瘋狂的旅程。我走進一間都是陌生人的房間，當時還不知道接下來這一年，我們會和這支隊伍一起拼命、把心都掏出來投入這個專題，留下這麼多回憶。在這支隊伍裡，我負責濕實驗和植物建模。整個專題期間我在實驗室待了超過 300 小時，操作這麼微量的試劑卻能做出像我們的光遺傳迴路這樣的東西，一直讓我覺得很神奇。這些結果不是一天來的，而是好幾個月的失敗與重建。我現在可以很自豪地說，我會做很多分子選殖技術，其中 Golden Gate 組裝和菌落 PCR 是我最喜歡的實驗。而我說這一整年是一趟瘋狂旅程，還因為我也養了小小的阿拉伯芥，幾乎把它們當成自己的寶寶。這也是我從農友的角度學到耐心這門功夫的時候：一點傾斜、一點碰觸、一點移動，都會影響它們的生長（或者就是黴菌調皮地長滿整個瓊脂培養盤）。但沒關係，我們變得更小心、更專業。因為每一支 iGEM 隊伍都是由 wetlab、drylab 和 hp 合成的一顆心，我也得到機會向教授、農友，甚至一位 iGEM 共同創辦人提案和報告；參與跨組的凝聚活動，和設計 clicker 這樣的支線任務；但最重要的是，和觀點與背景都很不一樣的人一起工作。一起笑過的那些時刻，永遠會是我 iGEM 旅程裡最亮的部分！

blocks.en: Hey everyone, I’m Gabriel, wet lab instructor. I’ll be guiding the biology experiments this year. Looking forward to learning a lot together over the coming months!
blocks.zh: 大家好，我是 Gabriel，濕實驗指導老師。今年我將引導生物學實驗，期待未來幾個月能和大家一起學習很多東西！

blocks.en: Hey, I'm Audrey Chu! My fascination with biology was the main reason I initially joined iGEM. Over this past year, however, I've read papers on protein mutations, designed hydroponic systems, managed and coded the wiki, and learned so much more. Moreover, reaching out to agricultural professionals and Taiwanese farmers shifted the way I looked at ReLEAF, from a simple plant project to a solution that could truly impact real people. Looking back now, my interest in biology is still strong as ever, but I also developed a passion for working with a team to make a vision come to life, to see so many different components come together into one big project. I'm looking forward to sharing what we did this year at the Jamboree in Paris, and no matter the outcome, I'm super grateful to have had this experience.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Audrey Chu！最初加入 iGEM，主要是因為我對生物學的著迷。不過在過去這一年裡，我讀了蛋白質突變的論文、設計水耕系統、管理並撰寫 wiki 的程式碼，還學到更多更多。此外，接觸農業領域的專業人士和臺灣農友，改變了我看 ReLEAF 的方式：它從一個單純的植物專題，變成一個真的能影響到活生生的人的解決方案。現在回頭看，我對生物學的興趣依然不減，但我也培養出另一種熱情：和一支隊伍合作，把一個願景變成真的，看著這麼多不同的環節匯聚成一個大專題。我很期待在巴黎的 Jamboree 上分享我們這一年做的事；無論結果如何，我都非常感謝能有這段經歷。

blocks.en: Hey, I'm Chloe! When people describe me in one word, they usually default to lazy. This is true, I am incredibly lazy. Being a part of this amazing team, building friendships and working on a project that I'm passionate about has taught me countless things. Turns out, I'm not incapable of hard work: I just needed to be truly driven by something I was dedicated to. At the beginning of my iGEM journey, I never expected to voluntarily trade my free time for endless cycles of colony PCR and golden gate assembly, but I now consider the lab my second home. Through failed transformations, unexpected contamination and troubleshooting protocols, I built a level of dedication I didn't know I had until I screamed out of excitement when we received our first successful sequencing results. Over the course of the summer and more than 300 hours spent in the lab, I went from having to double check every aspect of every procedure to being able to do miniprep from memory and claim the protocol on my labcoat. However, it was really the small acts of stepping out of the lab to interview small scale farmers alongside educating lower schoolers about the importance of rising climate change and how they affect agricultural resilience that really changed things for me, providing me a completely new level of motivation for our project. Our project ReLEAF isn't just relieving stress in plants, but rather, bringing relief to the farmers that rely on them, ensuring that every farmer can have their own bioreactor to combat plant stress step by step.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Chloe！如果要用一個詞形容我，大家通常會直接說懶。這是真的，我超級懶。而成為這支很棒的隊伍的一員、建立起友誼、投入一個自己有熱情的專題，教了我數不清的事。原來我不是沒有能力努力，我只是需要真的被某件自己全心投入的事推著走。在我 iGEM 旅程的開始，我從沒想過自己會自願把空閒時間換成沒完沒了的菌落 PCR 和 Golden Gate 組裝循環，但現在我把實驗室當成第二個家。經過失敗的轉形、意料外的污染和一次次排除流程問題，我累積出一種自己原本不知道有的投入；直到我們拿到第一次成功的定序結果時，我興奮地大叫出來。整個暑假、超過 300 小時待在實驗室，我從每個步驟都要反覆確認，變成可以憑記憶做 miniprep，把這份流程寫上自己的實驗衣。不過真正改變我的，其實是那些走出實驗室的小事：去訪談小農，同時向小學生講氣候變遷加劇有多重要、又如何影響農業的韌性。這些事給了我對專題全新的一層動力。我們的專題 ReLEAF 不只是舒緩植物的逆境，更是替依賴這些植物的農友帶來舒緩，讓每一位農友都能有自己的生物反應器，一步一步對抗植物逆境。

blocks.en: Hey, I'm Felix. I'm interested in biochemistry and engineering, but overall, I just like the satisfaction of seeing systems work. In the team, I specialize in protein design and software, while occasionally helping out with the hardware. A challenge in this pipeline is understanding the methodology of complex systems. As you try different docking tools and modeling approaches, you may realize after hours of work, on paper, it was all for nothing, and the process needed to be scrapped and re-done. However, each failure taught me to question my past assumptions, helping me approach the problem from a new perspective. Looking back, the team is also a system where things may break down in seemingly insignificant, unexpected places. With one part of the project greatly impacting another, over time, I’ve experienced the hardships of connecting pipelines, data, and people together. But I know we can work together and finish the job. I also have a fat dog and cat.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Felix。我對生物化學和工程很有興趣，但整體來說，我就是喜歡看到系統運作起來的那種滿足感。在隊伍裡，我專攻蛋白質設計和軟體，偶爾也幫忙硬體。這條流程裡的一個難處，是去理解複雜系統的方法學。當你試過不同的對接工具和建模方式，可能在花了好幾個小時之後才發現，在紙上這一切都白費了，整個過程得砍掉重做。但每一次失敗都教我去質疑自己過去的假設，幫我從新的角度切入問題。回頭看，隊伍本身也是一個系統，可能在看起來最不重要、最意想不到的地方壞掉。專題的一個環節會大大影響另一個環節，久而久之，我也嘗到了把流程、數據和人連在一起的辛苦。但我知道我們可以一起合作，把事情做完。另外，我有一隻胖狗和一隻胖貓。

blocks.en: Hey, I'm Sophie Chen! I’ve always loved chemistry, art, and math, so I didn’t expect to get this invested in synthetic biology, spending hundreds of hours in the lab. I joined iGEM wanting to create a worldwide impact, and somehow ended up looking forward to colony PCRs and liquid cultures. iGEM has really pushed my determination to chase results, not just for my own accomplishments, but for the team and everything we’ve worked on together. I mostly work in wetlab, but I’ve also enjoyed collaborating with drylab to understand the bigger picture and meeting with professors to hear different perspectives on our work. My favorite moments, though, are the messy ones: troubleshooting failed experiments, complaining about protocols, and interacting with teammates from completely different backgrounds. Somewhere along the way, iGEM made me realize that I don’t just like doing science: I really love being part of the process of figuring things out.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Sophie Chen！我一直很喜歡化學、藝術和數學，所以沒想到自己會這麼投入合成生物學，在實驗室待上好幾百個小時。我加入 iGEM 是想做出影響全世界的事，結果不知怎麼，變成每天期待菌落 PCR 和液體培養。iGEM 真的推著我更想追出結果，不只為了自己的成就，而是為了隊伍和我們一起做出來的一切。我主要待在 wetlab，但我也很喜歡和 drylab 合作，去看懂更大的全貌，以及去見教授、聽他們對我們工作的不同看法。不過我最喜歡的時刻，反而是那些亂的時刻：排除失敗實驗的問題、抱怨實驗流程，以及和背景完全不同的隊友互動。不知道從哪一刻開始，iGEM 讓我明白，我不只是喜歡做科學，我真的很愛成為把事情弄明白這個過程的一部分。

blocks.en: Hi everyone, I am Sara. I initially joined iGEM to look for my passion in synthetic Biology. The experience of transferring from wet lab to dry lab changes me a lot. Although transferring between groups is not common, I manage to find the similarities between these two labs. Even though I have a pretty rough time to catch up in dry lab, I think making decisions from two different perspectives of conducting experiment and prediction helps a lot. For example, I was in charge in plants when I was in wet lab. The experience of taking care of plants allows me to look for research for modules that correlated more to the conditions in lab. Overall, I realized the importance of communication and collaboration between labs to win or achieve our goals together.
blocks.zh: 大家好，我是 Sara。我最初加入 iGEM 是為了尋找自己對合成生物學的熱情。從濕實驗轉到乾實驗的經驗改變了我很多。雖然在組之間轉換並不常見，但我還是找到了這兩種實驗之間的相似處。即使我在乾實驗要跟上進度的那段時間相當辛苦，我覺得從做實驗和做預測這兩種不同角度來做決定，幫助很大。例如，我在濕實驗的時候負責植物。照顧植物的經驗讓我在找模組的研究時，更能挑出和實驗室條件更相關的。整體來說，我體會到實驗室之間溝通與合作的重要，我們才能一起贏、一起達成目標。

blocks.en: Hi! I’m Eva, a student interested in biology, medicine, and the ways science can be used to solve real-world problems. I joined iGEM to learn more about synthetic biology while working with my team to develop a creative solution to our project’s problem: plant stress.
blocks.zh: 嗨！我是 Eva，一個對生物學、醫學，以及科學能如何用來解決現實問題有興趣的學生。我加入 iGEM 是想多了解合成生物學，同時和隊伍一起為我們專題要處理的問題，也就是植物逆境，想出有創意的解決方案。

blocks.en: Hi! I’m Venus, a former project lead and wet-lab lead of the 2025 Gems Taiwan iGEM team. After an amazing experience last year, I chose to return as an advisor to support the 2026 team, share my wet-lab experience, and continue exploring the impact of synthetic biology together.
blocks.zh: 嗨！我是 Venus，2025 年 Gems Taiwan iGEM 隊伍的前專題負責人與濕實驗負責人。在去年一段很棒的經歷之後，我選擇以顧問的身份回來支持 2026 年的隊伍、分享我的濕實驗經驗，並繼續一起探索合成生物學的影響力。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Alex. I initially joined iGEM due to my interest and curiosity in synthetic biology. However, I found out that iGEM is way more than that. It involves collaboration, discussion, research, and many other things. Initially, my work mainly focused on the design of gene circuits, but I felt a little lost, and didn't really know what to do when I got to the lab. Later on, one of the instructors asked me to take care of plants for a while, and unexpectedly, I found my passion and love in taking care of plants. I started to participate much in plants, and without realizing, I transferred to the plant group. To be honest, I never thought of planting plants in my entire life. After lots of research on plants and some on protectants, as well as participating in interviews and meetings with experts, I became more familiar with plants. In the plant group, I learned to discuss and manage experiments, manage my time, and learned to solve problems when they occur. Through this project, I learned that iGEM was not only about synthetic biology, but also a process that explores new interests, working with others, overcome challenges. I am thankful for this year's experience.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Alex。我最初加入 iGEM 是出於對合成生物學的興趣和好奇。不過我發現 iGEM 遠不只如此，它包含合作、討論、研究，以及很多其他的事。一開始我的工作主要放在基因迴路的設計，但我有點迷失，進到實驗室也不太知道該做什麼。後來，其中一位指導老師請我照顧植物一段時間，沒想到我在照顧植物裡找到了自己的熱情和喜愛。我開始大量參與植物的工作，不知不覺就轉到了植物組。老實說，我這輩子從沒想過要種植物。在大量研究植物、也研究了一些保護劑，以及參與訪談和與專家的會議之後，我對植物更熟悉了。在植物組裡，我學會討論和安排實驗、管理自己的時間，也學會在問題發生時解決問題。透過這個專題，我學到 iGEM 不只關於合成生物學，也是一個探索新興趣、與他人合作、克服挑戰的過程。我很感謝這一年的經歷。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Anton. My background is in engineering and robotics, and I joined iGEM to see how those skills could carry over to synthetic biology and the problems it's trying to solve. This year, I designed and built an in-line photometer that tracked the optical density of our live B. subtilis cultures, along with an LED light plate for optogenetics assays. Through it all, I learned biology I had never studied before and spoke with professors and farmers about where our work could fit beyond the lab. I came in as an engineer and left with a much broader view of what it takes to build something meaningful. More than anything, I hope what we created doesn't stop here and finds its way to people who can put it to use. Outside of iGEM, I enjoy golf, traveling, and music.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Anton。我的背景是工程與機器人，加入 iGEM 是想看看這些能力能不能轉到合成生物學，以及它想解決的那些問題上。今年我設計並做出一台線上光度計，追蹤我們活的 B. subtilis 培養液的光密度，另外還做了一塊用於光遺傳檢測的 LED 光照板。這一路上，我學了以前從沒學過的生物學，也和教授、農友談過我們的工作在實驗室之外能放在哪裡。我以一個工程師的身份進來，離開時對「要做出有意義的東西需要什麼」有了寬得多的視野。最重要的是，我希望我們做出來的東西不要停在這裡，而能找到真正用得上它的人。iGEM 之外，我喜歡高爾夫、旅遊和音樂。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Ethan Liu! I was already THE PLANT GUY long before iGEM, so landing on a plant stress project felt extremely exciting. My math teachers always said math is the universal language. This is the first year I've watched it translate into millilitres in a farmer's bottle. Throughout the project, I've applied math to many fields, from creating a weather-stress model that directly predicts the yield of rice in the future to calculating how our protectant is uptaken by the leaves. Outside iGEM I grow, draw, and eat plants, which became suspiciously relevant once the whole model came down to it.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Ethan Liu！早在 iGEM 之前我就已經是「那個植物人」了，所以落到一個植物逆境的專題上，讓我覺得超級興奮。我的數學老師總說數學是世界的通用語言。今年是我第一次看著它被翻譯成農友瓶子裡的毫升數。整個專題期間，我把數學用在很多面向，從做出一個直接預測未來稻米產量的氣候逆境模型，到計算我們的保護劑如何被葉片吸收。iGEM 之外，我種植物、畫植物、吃植物，而這些在整個模型最後收斂到這裡時，變得可疑地相關。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Hachi, I was the project lead and wet-lab lead for Gems Taiwan 2025. My passion for synthetic biology has driven me to pursue iGEM for another round, but as an advisor to share experiences with new iGEMers. This year, instead of spending hours in the lab, I focused more on documenting the team's journey with my camera, from the small details in the lab to all the unseen efforts, I try to capture everything through my lens. I look forward to supporting and working with the team, and build a meaningful project.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Hachi，我曾是 Gems Taiwan 2025 的專題負責人與濕實驗負責人。對合成生物學的熱忱讓我再次參與 iGEM，但這次是以顧問的身份，和新的 iGEMer 分享經驗。今年我沒有花好幾個小時待在實驗室，而是更專注在用相機記錄隊伍的旅程，從實驗室裡的小細節到所有看不見的付出，我試著用鏡頭把一切拍下來。我期待能支持並與隊伍一起合作，做出一個有意義的專題。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Jacquelyn! I joined iGEM expecting a lot of lab work, PCR, cloning: the kind of science I was already used to. Instead, this project took me far outside the lab. I found myself kneeling in a farmer's field, talking with researchers at factories, speaking with professors, and hearing perspectives I never would have encountered if I had stayed inside the lab. I'm so grateful to have worked with so many people, especially my teammates, to build ReLEAF together.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Jacquelyn！加入 iGEM 的時候，我以為會有很多實驗室的工作、PCR、選殖，就是我本來已經熟悉的那種科學。結果這個專題把我帶到實驗室之外很遠的地方。我發現自己跪在農友的田裡、和工廠的研究人員談話、和教授對談，聽到如果我一直待在實驗室裡就絕對不會遇到的觀點。我非常感謝能和這麼多人，特別是我的隊友，一起把 ReLEAF 建起來。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Joshua. I love biology, firmware, and outdoor activities. When I first joined iGEM, I was excited about the possibility of doing experiments to create something impactful. However, I forgot that behind the achievements is sacrifice. These include repeating the same experiment countless times until cloning succeeds, or countless hours in labs or on computers. Throughout the year, I learned that patience and commitment are the cornerstones of research, and that really caring about and owning your tasks is what makes things work. Though I’m a wet lab member, most of my contribution lies in hardware. Prior to this experience, I never thought tech and bio could go hand in hand. It opened my eyes to new possibilities, since I now know I can combine my two interests. I really cherish this year and all the opportunities it provided. I learned a lot and found out more about myself. It is truly a surreal experience.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Joshua。我喜歡生物學、韌體和戶外活動。剛加入 iGEM 的時候，我很興奮能透過做實驗做出有影響力的東西。但我忘了，成果的背後是犧牲。這包括把同一個實驗重複無數次直到選殖成功，或是在實驗室和電腦前耗掉的無數小時。這一年我學到，耐心和投入是研究的基石，而真的在意並承擔起自己的任務，才是事情能動起來的原因。雖然我是濕實驗的成員，我大部分的貢獻其實在硬體。在這之前，我從沒想過科技和生物能並肩而行。這讓我看到新的可能，因為我現在知道自己可以把兩個興趣結合起來。我很珍惜這一年，以及它給我的所有機會。我學到很多，也更認識自己。這真的是一段超現實的經歷。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Neo! I was the project lead and dry-lab lead for GEMS Taiwan 2025, and my passion for engineering and synthetic biology brought me back for another round, this time as an advisor. This year I've been helping guide the project while working alongside the students, figuring things out with them when something doesn't work and sharing what I can from last year. I look forward to supporting the team and making this year's project a meaningful one.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Neo！我曾是 GEMS Taiwan 2025 的專題負責人與乾實驗負責人，對工程和合成生物學的熱忱帶我回來再走一輪，這次是以顧問的身份。今年我一邊協助引導專題，一邊和學生並肩工作，在事情不順的時候和他們一起把問題弄清楚，也盡量把去年的經驗分享出來。我期待能支持隊伍，讓今年的專題成為一個有意義的專題。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Noah Tau, and I joined iGEM to explore my growing passion for engineering. At first, that passion was limited to engineering and robotics. Through iGEM however, I was able to bring the skills I built in FRC into a new field and take on a real role in a project that offers tangible help for a real-world problem. At a symposium in Tainan, I presented our project, ReLEAF, to professors from Japan. Their questions pushed me to explain our work more clearly and to think harder about the science and logic behind it. That experience made the project feel like my own, and it taught me lessons about communication as well as scientific thinking that I could never have learned from a textbook at school. I came to iGEM as a robotics student curious about biology and am leaving as an engineer who knows skills beyond the field he started in. I'm excited to keep on progressing in the place where these two worlds meet.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Noah Tau，加入 iGEM 是為了探索自己對工程日漸增長的熱情。起初這份熱情只限於工程和機器人。但透過 iGEM，我把在 FRC 累積的能力帶進一個新的領域，在一個能為現實問題提供實際幫助的專題裡擔起真正的角色。在臺南的一場研討會上，我向來自日本的教授介紹我們的專題 ReLEAF。他們的問題逼著我把我們的工作講得更清楚，也更認真去想背後的科學和邏輯。那次經歷讓這個專題變成我自己的，也教了我在學校課本上永遠學不到的溝通與科學思考。我以一個對生物好奇的機器人學生身份進到 iGEM，離開時成了一個懂得本行之外能力的工程師。我很期待在這兩個世界交會的地方繼續往前。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Olivia! Given the chances I would get to work in both dry-lab and wet-lab settings, I joined iGEM. I'm so grateful to have met and worked with everyone here. I expected we'd make countless memories together, but nothing prepared me for the late-night writing, endless hours in the lab, and midnight meetings. I love that I had a chance to touch on the geospatial analysis, protein modeling/mutations, and wet lab sectors of this team project. I developed a well-rounded understanding of farmers' real challenges through geographical analysis, photos, interviews, and presentations rather than simply reading papers. Though our project's immediate impact on the world may not be huge, this year of endurance and grinding had a real impact on the farmers we touched and the team we formed. No matter the outcome, I am so happy to have joined iGEM and met all these hardworking people.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Olivia！因為能有機會同時接觸乾實驗和濕實驗，我加入了 iGEM。我很感謝能認識並和這裡的每一個人一起工作。我本來就預期我們會一起留下數不清的回憶，但沒有任何事能讓我為深夜的寫作、實驗室裡沒完沒了的時數和午夜的會議做好準備。我很喜歡自己有機會碰到這個團隊專題裡的地理空間分析、蛋白質建模與突變，以及濕實驗這幾個部分。我是透過地理分析、照片、訪談和報告，而不是單純讀論文，才對農友真正的難處有了全面的理解。雖然我們的專題對世界的即時影響也許不大，但這一年的撐持與硬磨，對我們接觸到的農友和我們組成的這支隊伍，確實帶來了影響。無論結果如何，我都很開心自己加入了 iGEM，認識了這些這麼努力的人。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Olivia! I joined iGEM because I wanted to explore my interest in biology and see how it connects to the real world. Being pretty shy and introverted, I was really unsure about stepping into Human Practices, where the whole job meant reaching out to people both on the team and far outside of it. Early on, managing outreach alongside school was a big adjustment. Over the months, I learned how to connect with external experts, help build a real business plan, and even spend a little time at the bench learning basic lab techniques. Presenting our project to professors and field experts showed me I could explain our work clearly and hold my own. Looking back, this year helped me step out of my comfort zone and showed me I can handle a lot more than I thought.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Olivia！我加入 iGEM 是因為想探索自己對生物學的興趣，看看它怎麼和現實世界連在一起。我個性比較害羞內向，所以對於要走進人文實踐真的很不確定，因為那份工作整件事就是去接觸人，隊伍裡的人和隊伍之外很遠的人都要。一開始，一邊處理對外推廣一邊應付學校是很大的調整。幾個月下來，我學會怎麼和外部專家建立聯繫、協助寫出一份真正的商業計畫，甚至花了一點時間在實驗檯邊學基本的實驗技術。向教授和田間專家報告我們的專題，讓我看到自己能把我們的工作講清楚、站得住腳。回頭看，這一年幫我走出舒適圈，也讓我看到自己能承擔的比想像中多得多。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Phoebe. Initially, I joined iGEM due to my passion for all things biology. Throughout the process, however, I realized that this competition was much more than conducting research and experiments. I learned to handle tools I've never heard of both digital and physical. I experimented with and solidified my understanding in the inner workings of a bioreactor and used online resources and codes to create math models and forecasting tools. These were all skills and knowledge I've never thought I'd acquire when I first joined this team. No matter the outcome when we eventually head to Paris, I'm thankful for this year-long journey and experience.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Phoebe。我最初加入 iGEM，是出於對所有生物學事物的熱情。不過在過程中，我發現這個競賽遠不只是做研究和實驗。我學會使用以前從沒聽過的工具，數位的和實體的都有。我動手試過、也紮實弄懂了生物反應器內部的運作，並用網路上的資源和程式碼做出數學模型與預報工具。這些都是我剛加入這支隊伍時從沒想過自己會學到的技能和知識。不管最後去到巴黎的結果如何，我都很感謝這一整年的旅程和經歷。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Renee and I initially joined iGEM because I want to learn more about biology and learn more about my own interest in it. Through the year-long journey I went through with the team, I initially struggled with maintaining a work-life balance and really getting into the mindset of putting my all into iGEM, but months later not only have I somehow maybe managed to find that balance, I've also learned to do things like GIS, hound people for work, and managing a business plan.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Renee，我最初加入 iGEM 是因為想多了解生物學，也想多了解自己對它的興趣。在和隊伍一起走過這一整年的旅程裡，我一開始很難維持工作與生活的平衡，也很難真的進入把全部的自己投入 iGEM 的狀態；但幾個月後，我不只好像勉強找到了那個平衡，還學會了做 GIS、追著別人交工作，以及管理一份商業計畫。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Ryan Wei! I joined iGEM simply to pursue my interest in synthetic biology. The competition, however, struck me as much more than what I expected: beyond the incredible experience of working in a lab independently as a high school student, the connections and communication between members, instructors, and advisors, the collaborative work between different groups, the public engagement initiatives, and even guidance from professors we didn't know at the start of the competition really strike me as something very realistic and reminiscent of what an actual, authentic research project looks like. I am very grateful for the opportunity I have been given to explore and learn more about synthetic biology in the future.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Ryan Wei！我加入 iGEM 只是為了追求自己對合成生物學的興趣。但這個競賽給我的衝擊遠超出我的預期：除了身為高中生能獨立在實驗室工作這段很了不起的經歷之外，成員、指導老師與顧問之間的連結與溝通、不同組之間的協作、公眾參與的行動，甚至來自競賽開始時我們還不認識的教授的指導，都讓我覺得非常真實，很像一個真正、名副其實的研究專題。我非常感謝自己得到這個機會，能在未來繼續探索並更了解合成生物學。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Ryan Yuan. I joined iGEM out of curiosity, influenced by a friend, and soon fell in love with synthetic biology. When I first joined the team, I was primarily interested in wet lab experiments and believed that wet lab work was the core of an iGEM project. However, as time passed, I came to realize that dry lab, human practices, and even video editing can carry the same weight for a successful iGEM team. iGEM taught me to step up for my team, take responsibility for my actions, and embrace uncertainty with an open mind. One example was video editing, something completely unfamiliar to me. Before iGEM, I had never even opened video editing software. When the team needed someone to take on the task, I stepped up and took responsibility. I spent hours figuring out how to edit, going through hundreds of sound effects and transitions, and talking to people I normally would not interact with to gather key information and structure the video properly. I also developed a greater sense of attentiveness by constantly trying to make the video as smooth and polished as possible. It had little to do with wet lab experiments, yet I felt more accomplished than I ever had before. That experience showed me that contributing to iGEM is not limited to the field I initially expected to pursue. It is about being willing to step outside your comfort zone, learn something completely new, and contribute wherever the team needs you.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Ryan Yuan。我因為好奇、受朋友影響而加入 iGEM，很快就愛上了合成生物學。剛進隊伍的時候，我主要對濕實驗感興趣，也以為濕實驗的工作就是一個 iGEM 專題的核心。但隨著時間過去，我才明白乾實驗、人文實踐，甚至影片剪輯，對一支成功的 iGEM 隊伍都能有同樣的份量。iGEM 教我為隊伍站出來、為自己的行為負責，並以開放的心態接受不確定。其中一個例子就是影片剪輯，一件我完全不熟的事。在 iGEM 之前，我連剪輯軟體都沒打開過。當隊伍需要有人接下這個任務時，我站了出來、承擔起責任。我花了好幾個小時摸索怎麼剪，翻過上百個音效和轉場，也去找平常不會互動的人聊，蒐集關鍵資訊、把影片的結構安排好。我也因為一直想把影片做得更順、更精緻，而培養出更強的細心。這和濕實驗幾乎無關，但我感受到的成就感卻比以前任何時候都大。那次經歷讓我看到，對 iGEM 的貢獻並不限於我原本以為自己會走的領域。它關乎的是願意走出舒適圈、學一件全新的事，並在隊伍需要的地方貢獻自己。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Sarah~ I am very interested in experiments and biology. The hardest part of iGEM for me was seeing no band where I expected one on my PCR gel. I had followed the procedure, so at first I did not know what had gone wrong. Instead of repeating the experiment without a plan, I went back to the plasmid map, calculated the expected fragment size, checked the primer positions, and compared the result with the DNA ladder. I discussed possible causes with my teammates before deciding what to try next. In January, I needed help understanding what a gel result meant. Now I can use a plasmid map to predict a band size and think through possible reasons when an experiment fails. I have also learned to keep clearer lab notes so the team can use each result, even an unsuccessful one. The missing band was frustrating, but it taught me that research involves asking better questions after an experiment does not go as expected.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Sarah～我對實驗和生物學非常有興趣。對我來說，iGEM 最難的部分是在自己的 PCR 膠上，原本該出現條帶的位置卻什麼都沒有。我是照著流程做的，所以一開始我不知道哪裡出了問題。我沒有毫無計畫地重做一次實驗，而是回到質體圖譜，計算預期的片段大小、檢查引子的位置，並把結果和 DNA 標準品比對。我在決定下一步要試什麼之前，先和隊友討論可能的原因。一月的時候，我還需要別人幫我看懂一張膠的結果代表什麼。現在我可以用質體圖譜預測條帶的大小，並在實驗失敗時把可能的原因想過一遍。我也學會把實驗紀錄寫得更清楚，讓隊伍能用上每一個結果，就算是失敗的結果也一樣。那條不見的條帶很令人沮喪，但它教了我：研究就是在實驗沒照預期走之後，問出更好的問題。

blocks.en: Hi, I'm Sophie Huang. Initially, I joined the iGEM competition for a chance to get closer to Biology, one of my favorite subjects. At first, I envisioned synthetic biology as a pristine world of precise equations and predictable organisms. But stepping into our Biomanufacturing project with GEMS-Taiwan quickly showed me that living systems are far more dynamic, and delightfully chaotic, than anything in a textbook. Throughout this journey, I’ve navigated the intricate bridge between concept and application, learning that real scientific impact requires both rigorous technical execution and a clear vision for how biomanufactured solutions touch the real world. Beyond the lab bench and project timelines, the steep learning curve tested my adaptability and resilience. I learned how to embrace unexpected design pivots, align diverse ideas across a multi-faceted team, and turn abstract biological challenges into functional, scalable outcomes. Looking back, this experience transformed my curiosity into confidence, proving that high school researchers can actively contribute to the future of biotechnology. I’m incredibly proud of what our team has built, and I can't wait to share our work at the Grand Jamboree!
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Sophie Huang。最初我參加 iGEM 競賽，是想有機會更靠近生物學，我最喜歡的科目之一。一開始，我把合成生物學想成一個由精確方程式和可預測生物組成的乾淨世界。但一走進我們和 GEMS-Taiwan 的生物製造專題，我很快就發現，活的系統遠比課本裡的任何東西都更動態，也混亂得可愛。這一路上，我走過概念與應用之間那座複雜的橋，學到真正的科學影響力同時需要嚴謹的技術執行，以及對生物製造方案如何觸及現實世界的清楚願景。除了實驗檯和專題進度之外，陡峭的學習曲線也考驗了我的適應力與韌性。我學會接受意料外的設計轉向、在一支多面向的隊伍裡整合各種不同的想法，並把抽象的生物挑戰變成可運作、可放大的成果。回頭看，這段經歷把我的好奇變成了自信，證明高中生的研究也能實際為生物科技的未來做出貢獻。我非常驕傲我們隊伍做出來的東西，也等不及要在 Grand Jamboree 上分享我們的工作！

blocks.en: Hi, I’m Audrey Hsieh. I joined the iGEM competition to explore my passion for synthetic biology and challenge myself through hands-on research. When I first joined iGEM, I thought I would mainly be learning about synthetic biology and contributing to a research project. Instead, the experience took me far beyond the lab. I found myself approaching problems from different perspectives, and working with people who challenged me to grow. Speaking with farmers and studying their experiences helped me understand that solving a scientific problem also requires understanding the people affected by it.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Audrey Hsieh。我參加 iGEM 競賽是為了探索自己對合成生物學的熱情，並透過動手做研究挑戰自己。剛加入 iGEM 的時候，我以為自己主要會是在認識合成生物學、為一個研究專題出力。結果這段經歷把我帶到實驗室之外很遠的地方。我發現自己開始從不同的角度切入問題，也和那些推著我成長的人一起工作。和農友談話、研究他們的經驗，讓我明白解決一個科學問題，同時也需要理解被這個問題影響的人。

blocks.en: Hi, I’m Dylan! I joined iGEM as an advisor because I’m interested in synthetic biology and enjoy projects that connect engineering and biology. This year, I’ve been involved in extensive Human Practices outreach, building connections with experts and professionals, while sharing both drylab and wet lab advice and provide assistance based on my experience from last year. I helped to document the team's progress by capturing small details of our work through photography. I hope to support the team in bringing its ideas to life and making this year’s iGEM journey a meaningful one!
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Dylan！我以顧問的身份加入 iGEM，因為我對合成生物學有興趣，也喜歡連結工程與生物學的專題。今年我大量參與人文實踐的對外推廣，和專家與業界人士建立聯繫，同時依據我去年的經驗提供乾實驗與濕實驗兩方面的建議與協助。我也透過攝影記錄下我們工作裡的小細節，幫忙把隊伍的進展留下來。我希望能支持隊伍把想法變成真的，讓今年的 iGEM 旅程成為一段有意義的旅程！

blocks.en: Hi, I’m Naomi! I joined iGEM because I was fascinated by synthetic biology and wanted to experience real research. I expected to spend most of my time doing labs and reading papers, but iGEM became much more than that. Throughout the year, I learned to turn biology concepts into experiments, balance iGEM with schoolwork, and work with teammates from different schools. When I made mistakes, I learned to face them honestly, learn from them, and step up again. I also learned to look beyond my own role and see how different parts of a project connect, and this is why I enjoy cross-team work. I even brought ReLEAF to my school by coordinating with my teachers and teammates to organize an educational event, allowing my peers a chance to learn about synthetic biology and its role in addressing agricultural challenges. Through ReLEAF, I came to see research as a way to share knowledge and address problems beyond the lab.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Naomi！我加入 iGEM 是因為被合成生物學吸引，也想體驗真正的研究。我以為自己大部分時間會花在做實驗和讀論文，但 iGEM 遠不只如此。這一年，我學會把生物學的概念變成實驗、在 iGEM 和學校功課之間取得平衡，並和來自不同學校的隊友合作。犯錯的時候，我學會誠實面對、從中學習，然後再站起來。我也學會把眼光放到自己的角色之外，看見一個專題的不同部分如何彼此相連，這也是我喜歡跨組工作的原因。我甚至和老師與隊友協調，在自己的學校辦了一場教育活動，把 ReLEAF 帶進校園，讓同學有機會認識合成生物學，以及它在面對農業挑戰上扮演的角色。透過 ReLEAF，我開始把研究看成一種在實驗室之外分享知識、處理問題的方式。

blocks.en: Hi, I’m Sophia! I’ve always been interested in biology, which is one of the reasons I decided to join iGEM. Throughout the year, I’ve learned and experienced many new things, including designing an educational lesson, helping build a business plan, contacting experts, organizing outreach events, learning lab techniques, and much more than I ever imagined I would learn if I hadn’t joined iGEM. I’m looking forward to present our results and share the insights we’ve gained throughout this journey. I hope to carry the knowledge and experiences I’ve gained from iGEM into my future studies and continue exploring biology and science.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Sophia！我一直對生物學有興趣，這也是我決定加入 iGEM 的原因之一。這一年，我學到也經歷了很多新的事，包括設計一堂教育課程、協助建立商業計畫、聯繫專家、籌辦對外推廣活動、學習實驗技術，還有更多我如果沒加入 iGEM 就想像不到自己會學到的東西。我很期待能報告我們的成果，分享這一路上得到的體會。我希望能把從 iGEM 得到的知識與經驗帶進未來的學習，繼續探索生物學與科學。

blocks.en: Hi, I’m Sophie! I joined iGEM to explore synthetic biology and build practical scientific skills. Over the past year, I learned to troubleshoot and adapt when experiments and processes didn’t go as planned, or when our initial assumptions about market promotion were wrong I worked across wet lab, drylab hardware/math modeling, and business strategy, constantly shifting between different types of problems. Through focusing on cross-team work and understanding how each workflow fed into others, I really got to understand how much of the project’s success depended on people communicating with each other and building on what different subteams had learned. The most valuable part of this experience was learning from professors, farmers we interviewed, as well as collaborating with the instructors and my teammates, and each person in this journey has taught me something different about what it takes to build a project that will actually be successful in the real world, which I’m extremely grateful to be able to experience.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Sophie！我加入 iGEM 是為了探索合成生物學，建立實用的科學技能。過去這一年，我學會在實驗和流程不如預期、或我們一開始對市場推廣的假設是錯的時候，排除問題並調整做法。我橫跨濕實驗、drylab 的硬體與數學建模，以及商業策略，不斷在不同類型的問題之間切換。因為把重心放在跨組工作、也去理解每一條工作流程如何餵進另一條，我真正體會到這個專題的成功有多大一部分取決於人與人之間的溝通，以及在各個分組學到的東西上繼續往上建。這段經歷最有價值的部分，是向教授和我們訪談過的農友學習，以及和指導老師、隊友一起合作；這趟旅程裡的每一個人，都教了我一些不同的東西，關於要做出一個在現實世界裡真正成功的專題需要什麼，我非常感謝自己能有這樣的經歷。

blocks.en: Hi, this is Gina, one of wetlab instructors. I passionate about science and have extensive hands-on experience working in lab. Also I enjoy guiding students in hands-on experiments.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Gina，濕實驗指導老師之一。我對科學充滿熱情，有豐富的實驗室實作經驗，也很享受帶領學生進行動手操作的實驗。

blocks.en: Hii, I'm Abby Kao! My main interests are ballet and public speaking, yet it was my interest in biology that led me to join iGEM. Through the hundreds of hours I have spent with these (initial) strangers in the lab, I realized that through one year of locked in dedication, we could really achieve something big. Overall, I played a role in conducting the cross-team aspect of our team, and, looking at the map of our project, I understand everything that plays a role leading to our success. Whether it is video editing, testing our protectant of arabidopsis, educating elementary school students and the general public, interviewing farmers, doing golden gate assembly, or designing merch, nothing goes unnoticed, and honestly? It's the best feeling ever knowing almost 100 people are working towards the same goal. Even though it looks like summer 2026 wasted, it was a summer full of the best experiences, spending it with the best people as well as learning from and laughing at our mistakes. While our arabidopsis grew, we grew with hope and anticipation, not for what contamination would appear next, but for next time we could test another protectant on our plants and the next time we get to share our project with the outside world.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Abby Kao！我主要的興趣是芭蕾和公開演說，不過真正把我帶進 iGEM 的，是我對生物學的興趣。和這些（起初的）陌生人在實驗室一起度過幾百個小時之後，我發現只要一年全心投入，我們真的可以做到很大的事。整體來說，我在隊伍裡負責跨組的部分；看著我們專題的全圖，我理解每一件通往成功的事。不論是影片剪輯、在阿拉伯芥上測試我們的保護劑、向小學生和一般民眾做教育、訪談農友、做 Golden Gate 組裝，還是設計周邊，沒有一件會被忽略；而且老實說？知道將近 100 個人正朝著同一個目標努力，是最棒的感覺。雖然看起來像是浪費了 2026 年的暑假，但那是一個充滿最棒經歷的暑假，和最棒的人一起度過，也從自己的錯誤裡學習、笑自己的錯誤。在我們的阿拉伯芥長大的同時，我們也帶著希望和期待一起長大；期待的不是下一個污染會是什麼，而是下一次能在植物上測試另一種保護劑，以及下一次能把我們的專題分享給外面的世界。

blocks.en: Hiii I'm Abigail! I love solving mystery novels, and to me, the plant world is the ultimate unsolved case. Outside of biology, I enjoy painting, diving, and scouting. At the beginning of the year, I came with basic biology knowledge, a very ambitious heart, and a wild project idea. Now, after months of plant experiments, failed protocols, contamination, and countless trips to the lab straight after school, I can navigate the bench much more confidently. During the summer alone, I spent over 100 hours each month in lab, often sacrificing "fun" time but allowing me to perform cloning without constantly staring at my notebook for every step, troubleshooting experiments, and even planning test trials independently. I originally came up with our project sitting in front of a cold computer, researching the struggles of farmers facing an increasingly unpredictable climate. Field visits, small scale farmers' interviews, and public forums made those struggles real to me. I saw not only the interactions between technology and humans, but nature's and human's cooperation; to see the struggles, adaptations, and losses happening in front of my eyes made me strengthen my determination to develop our project. Attending the International Symposium of Living Systems was especially memorable to me because presenting our work alongside passionate scientists made me feel that I had stepped into the larger scientific community, sharing the love for science together. Throughout this journey, I designed our topic, logo, and visuals, but I think we finally discovered what our project represents; “releaf": not only relieving the stress of plants, but also the stress carried by the people who grow our food.
blocks.zh: 嗨，我是 Abigail！我喜歡解謎小說，對我來說，植物的世界就是最終極的未解之謎。生物學之外，我喜歡畫畫、潛水和童軍。年初的時候，我帶著基本的生物學知識、一顆非常有野心的心，和一個很狂的專題想法來。現在，經過好幾個月的植物實驗、失敗的流程、污染，以及數不清放學後直接衝去實驗室的日子，我在實驗檯前自在多了。光是整個暑假，我每個月在實驗室待超過 100 小時，常常犧牲掉「好玩」的時間，但也因此能在不必每一步都盯著筆記的情況下做選殖、排除實驗問題，甚至獨立規劃測試性的試驗。我們的專題最初是我坐在冷冰冰的電腦前想出來的，當時我在研究農友面對越來越難預測的氣候時的困境。田間走訪、小農訪談和公開論壇，讓那些困境對我變得真實。我看到的不只是科技與人的互動，還有自然與人的合作；看著困境、調適與損失在我眼前發生，讓我更堅定要把我們的專題做下去。參加 International Symposium of Living Systems 對我特別難忘，因為和充滿熱情的科學家一起報告我們的工作，讓我覺得自己踏進了更大的科學社群，一起分享對科學的愛。這一路上，我設計了我們的主題、標誌和視覺；但我想我們終於發現了我們的專題代表什麼：「releaf」，不只舒緩植物的逆境，也舒緩種出我們糧食的那些人所承受的逆境。

blocks.en: Howdy! Pak here (yes, I lived in Houston for a few years). This is my first year with iGEM, and what an eye-opener! Between the high level of science, the dedication of both instructors and students, and an amazing sense of curiosity, it’s been an incredible ride. As a newcomer to synbio, I’ve learned right alongside the team. Having worked in both academia and industrial R&D, watching these budding scientists tackle such challenging issues is truly rewarding and inspiring.
blocks.zh: 嗨！我是 Pak（是的，我在休士頓住過幾年）。這是我參與 iGEM 的第一年，真是大開眼界！科學的水準、指導老師與學生的投入，還有一種了不起的好奇心，這一路都很精彩。作為合成生物學的新手，我是和隊伍一起邊做邊學的。我在學界和產業研發都待過，看著這些初出茅廬的科學家處理這麼有挑戰性的題目，真的既有收穫也很激勵人。

blocks.en: This group pitched the idea before anyone knew it would become a project, became the gravity that pulled the team together when it was 32 strangers from seven schools, drove our cloning progress without needing instructors to walk them through it step by step, strung our project results together toward a larger synbio vision, and brought our bioreactor in front of academic experts and field farmers. ReLEAF is relieved to have them.
blocks.zh: 這群人在沒有人知道這會變成一個專題之前就先提出了這個想法；在隊伍還只是來自七所學校的 32 個陌生人時，成為把大家聚在一起的重力；在不需要指導老師一步一步帶的情況下推著我們的選殖進度往前；把我們的專題成果串成一個更大的合成生物學願景；並把我們的生物反應器帶到學術專家和田間農友面前。有他們在，ReLEAF 鬆了一口氣。

blocks.en: This year we put plants under stress and watch who breaks first, sometimes it’s the system, sometimes it’s us. That’s fine. Not everything survives hardships. But often times that’s how you find the gems.
blocks.zh: 今年我們讓植物承受逆境，看看誰先撐不住，有時是系統，有時是我們自己。沒關係。不是所有事物都能熬過逆境。但往往就是在這個過程中，才能找到真正的珍寶。

blocks.en: We appreciate the contributions of the following members from the 2025 team.
blocks.zh: 我們感謝以下 2025 年隊伍成員的貢獻。
濕實驗指導老師

blocks.en: Worked through dry lab training: literature review, research methods, data analysis, wiki coding, protein design, math modelling, economic analysis, geospatial analysis and scientific writing. Takes a task from design through experiment and data analysis to the presented result, without supervision.
blocks.zh: 完成乾實驗訓練：文獻回顧、研究方法、數據分析、wiki 程式撰寫、蛋白質設計、數學建模、經濟分析、地理空間分析與科學寫作。能在無人監督的情況下，把一項任務從設計、實驗、數據分析一路帶到呈現出來的結果。

blocks.en: Worked through outreach writing, education material planning, entrepreneurship case studies and event hosting, and can run an event start to finish.
blocks.zh: 完成對外推廣寫作、教育教材規劃、創業案例研究與活動主持，並且能從頭到尾辦完一場活動。
